'''Samuel Kelley Forstag'''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.legistorm.com/person/bio/589715/Samuel_Kelley_Forstag.html|title=Sam Forstag - D Montana, 1st, Candidate - Biography |publisher=legistorm.com |date=2023 |access-date=2026-10-19}}</ref> (born May 23, 1994) is an American [[Labor unions in the United States|labor union]] leader and former [[smokejumper]] who is the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana#District 1|2026 election]] for [[Montana's 1st congressional district]] in the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]].<ref name="NYT 2026-06-03">{{Cite news |last=Mazzei |first=Patricia |date=June 3, 2026 |title=Former Smoke Jumper Wins Democratic House Primary in Montana |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/03/us/politics/montana-democratic-house-busse-forstag-rains.html |work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Woodall |first=Hunter |date=January 5, 2026 |title=Democrats are talking about a midterm blue wave. A Montana smokejumper could help make it a reality. |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/democrats-blue-wave-montana-first-congressional-district-sam-forstag/ |publisher=CBS News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sainato |first=Michael |date=February 20, 2026 |title=Smokejumper and union leader aims to win in Montana by focusing on workers |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/feb/20/sam-forstag-montana-workers |work=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite instagram |user=samforstag |postid=DYsmlJoEsUk |date=May 23, 2026 |title=It's my birthday today, and I want to take a second to say thank you. |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DYsmlJoEsUk/?img_index=1}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Forstag was born in [[Ohio]],<ref name="AKS">{{Cite news |last=Kimbel-Sannit |first=Arren |date=April 27, 2026 |title=Four brands of Democrat make their case in Montana's western congressional primary |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/04/27/four-brands-of-democrat-make-their-case-in-montanas-western-congressional-primary/ |work=[[Montana Free Press]] |access-date=June 27, 2026}}</ref> and raised mostly by a single mother who worked as an [[Critical care nursing|ICU nurse]] in [[Portland, Oregon]].<ref name="Esquire 2026-05-12">{{Cite news |last=Randall |first=Cassidy |date=May 12, 2026 |title=The Wildfire-Fighting Union Leader Who Could Change Montana Politics |url=https://www.esquire.com/news-politics/a71269113/sam-forstag-democratic-candidate-montana-house-smokejumper/ |work=Esquire |quote=}}</ref> He was raised [[Roman Catholic]], though his father's family is [[Jewish]] of [[Latvian Jews|Latvian]] origin.<ref name="jdca-endorse">{{cite web|url=https://jewishdems.org/endorsements/|title=JDCA Endorsed Candidates|publisher=Jewish Democratic Council of America|access-date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>

Forstag moved to Montana in 2012,<ref name="AKS"/> and worked multiple jobs to pay for his undergraduate education at the [[University of Montana]], where he studied [[philosophy]] and [[political science]] and was elected [[student body president]].<ref name="Esquire 2026-05-12" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Amestoy |first=Austin |date=March 31, 2026 |title=Q&A: Sam Forstag, Democratic western district U.S. House candidate |url=https://www.mtpr.org/montana-news/2026-03-31/sam-forstag-interview |publisher=Montana Public Radio}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating in 2017, Forstag took a job as a [[wildland firefighter]] to pay off [[Student debt|student loan debt]], intending to apply to [[law school]].<ref name="Esquire 2026-05-12" /> Instead he served as a wildland firefighter for eight years, including four years as a smokejumper.<ref name="KPAX 20216-06-03" /><ref name="Pulp 2026-02-02" /> During the off-seasons, he worked as an organizer and [[Lobbying|lobbyist]] for the Montana chapter of the [[American Civil Liberties Union]] and for lobbying group Central House Strategies, where he represented the city of [[Missoula, Montana|Missoula]].<ref name="Pulp 2026-02-02">{{Cite news |last=Kimbel-Sannit |first=Arren |date=February 2, 2026 |title=Schvitzing with Sam Forstag |url=https://thepulp.org/schvitzing-with-montana-congressional-candidate-sam-forstag/ |work=Pulp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Drew |first=Micah |date=2026-01-05 |title=Missoula smokejumper, union leader enters race for Congress |url=https://dailymontanan.com/2026/01/05/missoula-smokejumper-union-leader-enters-race-for-congress/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=Daily Montanan |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2025, he became vice president of the [[National Federation of Federal Employees]] (NFFE) Local 60, where he represents approximately 800 [[United States Forest Service|U.S. Forest Service]] workers.<ref name="Esquire 2026-05-12" /><ref name="Smokejumpers 2026-01-10">{{Cite web |date=January 10, 2026 |title=Sam Forstag Launches Congressional Bid |url=https://smokejumpers.com/sam-forstag-launches-congressional-bid/ |publisher=National Smokejumper Association}}</ref>

==2026 campaign==
As the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] nominee in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Montana#District 1|2026 election for the Montana 1st congressional district]] in the [[U.S. House of Representatives]], Forstag faced [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee [[Aaron Flint]] and [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] nominee Nick Sheedy.<ref name="KPAX 20216-06-03">{{Cite news |last=Brown |first=Emily |date=June 3, 2026 |title=Forstag secures democratic nomination for Western Montana Congressional District |url=https://www.kpax.com/news/montana-legislature/forstag-secures-democratic-nomination-for-western-montana-congressional-district |publisher=[[KPAX-TV]] |location=Missoula}}</ref> The winner will replace incumbent Republican [[Ryan Zinke]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Yilek |first=Caitlin |date=June 3, 2026 |title=Sam Forstag wins Democratic primary in Montana's 1st Congressional District, CBS News projects |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/montana-congressional-district-1-democratic-primary-results-sam-forstag/ |publisher=CBS News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=May 28, 2026 |title=Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Campaigns for Montana House Candidate Sam Forstag |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/campaign-2026/rep-alexandria-ocasio-cortez-campaigns-for-montana-house-candidate-sam-forstag/680056 |publisher=C-SPAN}}</ref>

Forstag's congressional campaign focused on protecting [[Public lands in the United States|public land]], alongside economic issues such as housing and health care affordability.<ref name="NYT 2026-06-03" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Dapcevich |first=Madison |date=June 3, 2026 |title=Sam Forstag Jumps out of Planes Fighting Wildfires. He Just Won Montana's Democratic Primary. |url=https://www.outsideonline.com/outdoor-adventure/environment/sam-forstag-montana/ |work=Outside}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Juhlin |first=Ellis |date=May 29, 2026 |title=In Missoula, Forstag and Ocasio-Cortez campaign for working class votes |url=https://www.mtpr.org/montana-news/2026-05-29/in-missoula-forstag-and-ocasio-cortez-campaign-for-working-class-votes |publisher=Montana Public Radio}}</ref> He was endorsed by union groups and national [[Progressivism|progressive]] leaders, including Senator [[Bernie Sanders]] and Representative [[Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Drew |first=Micah |date=June 2, 2026 |title=Forstag declares victory in U.S. House district in western Montana |url=https://dailymontanan.com/2026/06/02/busse-forstag-in-tight-race-among-four-way-democratic-primary-matchup/ |archive-url= |work=Daily Montanan}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Fairbanks |first=Katie |date=May 28, 2026 |title=Will Ocasio-Cortez's rally for Forstag matter? |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/05/28/will-ocasio-cortezs-rally-for-forstag-matter/ |work=Montana Free Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Mabie |first=Nora |last2=Lloyd |first2=Zeke |last3=Lutey |first3=Tom |last4=Olness |first4=Jacob |date=June 5, 2026 |title=What the June 2 primary results tell us about politics in Montana |url=https://montanafreepress.org/2026/06/05/5-takeaways-montana-primary-election/ |work=Montana Free Press}}</ref> He was endorsed by the [[Blue Dog PAC]], a coalition of moderate Democrats.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blue Dog PAC Endorses Six New Candidates Built to Win in Competitive Districts - Blue Dog PAC |url=https://bluedogdems.com/blue-dog-pac-endorses-six-new-candidates-built-to-win-in-competitive-districts/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=bluedogdems.com/ |language=en-US}}</ref> Forstag was also endorsed by Representative [[Susie Lee]], who is his aunt.<ref name="Smokejumpers 2026-01-10" />
